prerequisites: Basic prior knowledge of chemistry at least at the 4th year of E.S.O. level, including familiarity with basic chemical formulation and nomenclature, as well as aspects such as matter structure, atom, mole, stoichiometry, concentration units, chemical reactions, and the periodic table.
Knowledge of chemistry at the second year of high school level in the Science and Technology modality is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Relate the principles of basic chemistry knowledge to their use in various industrial processes derived from them.
Know the basic principles of organic chemistry and their application in industrial processes.
Know the basic principles of inorganic chemistry and their application in industrial processes.

syllabus_topics: Structure of matter. Classification and periodic properties.
The atom and radioactivity. Industrial applications of radioactivity.
The chemical bond and its relationship with the structure of matter.
Reaction rate. Catalysts and their industrial use.
Organic chemistry. Mechanisms of organic chemical reactions.

Basic chemical formulation and nomenclature (organic and inorganic), including main inorganic compounds (binary compounds, acids, ions, hydroxides, oxides, salts and addition compounds) and organic compounds (hydrocarbons and main functional groups with single or multiple bonds).
ATOMIC THEORY AND COMPOSITION OF THE ATOM
Atomic number and mass number. Isotopes
Solutions: units of concentration; principles of solubility
Electron distribution and the periodic system
Ionic bond. Lattice energy. Born-Haber cycle
Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion Theory (VSEPR)
Some basic concepts: enthalpy (H), entropy (S) and Gibbs energy (G)
Indirect determination of ΔH: Hess's law
Reaction rate. Factors affecting reaction rate
Dependence on the nature of reactants and products. Activation energy
Equilibria in the gas phase. Ideal gas law. Dalton's law
The equilibrium constant. Kc and Kp
Changes in external conditions: Le Chatelier's Principle. Effect of concentration, volume (or pressure) and temperature variation
Gibbs energy and equilibrium constant. Dependence of the equilibrium constant on temperature.
Calculation of solubility from Kps. Common ion effect
ACIDS AND BASES. ACID-BASE EQUILIBRIA IN AQUEOUS SOLUTION
Strength of acids and bases. Ionization constants of weak acids and bases (Ka and Kb)
Autoionization of water (Kw). pH and pOH
Dissociation of strong and weak acids and bases
Hydrolysis of salts. Prediction of a salt's pH in water
Oxidation numbers. Balancing redox reactions by the ion-electron method
Electrode potentials and their measurement. Standard reduction potentials
Batteries and cells: obtaining electricity through chemical reactions
SESSION 1: Laboratory safety. Handling glassware. Handling reagents and solvents.
SESSION 2: Methods for separating chemical substances.
SESSION 3: Organic synthesis: synthesis of biodiesel and a polymer (Nylon).
SESSION 4: Acid-base reactions: indicators and acid-base titration.

assessment_methods.method: Lab reports and practical work reports

assessment_rules: Attendance to practical sessions is mandatory for evaluating the lab reports grade. It is essential to pass the Formulation and Nomenclature test, which requires at least 70% correct answers; failure to do so will result in a maximum overall grade of 4.5 (SUSPENSO). Students must obtain at least 4 out of 10 in the final written exam (or the second partial exam for those who passed the first partial); failure to do so will result in a maximum overall grade of 4.5 (SUSPENSO). A partial exam can liberate corresponding material if a score of 5 out of 10 is achieved, but this score is only valid for the first call.
